problem: Zero-shot VLN navigators with strong semantic planning still fail at spatially constrained transitions (stairs): reaching a staircase does not ensure traversal. Waypoint hierarchies encode where the agent can move, not an instruction-conditioned pose to execute from, and imitation policies suffer compounding errors beyond expert states.
motivation: Stair traversal is a major source of failures in multi-floor navigation (~21% of failures per prior work), and VLMs are weak at 3D/action-induced spatial reasoning. The authors call the remaining disconnect between geometric localization and an agent-centric executable pose the 'semantic-spatial gap'. A local module conditioned on a traversable affordance pose, and trained on its own failures, could bridge it in a plug-and-play way.
key_idea: PACE predicts an agent-centric traversable affordance pose and traversal phase from RGB-D and VLM direction guidance, conditions short-horizon action generation on it, and is post-trained with failure-aware preference pairs (normal/recovery vs deviation snippets), as a plug-in for frozen zero-shot navigators.
insight: Conditioning the action decoder directly on the affordance representation matters: removing conditioning drops OSR by 13.5 points, using affordance only as auxiliary supervision drops it by 18.1, and action-only BC trails by 49.9. Failure-aware refinement (on-policy rollouts + A* recovery + preference loss) is also crucial: removing it costs 30.1 OSR points, and the preference loss alone accounts for 10.9. Gains come mostly from stair-transition episodes, so the module is local rather than improving global instruction following.
method: Affordance state: agent-centric pose (x,y,θ) giving the entry pose before traversal and the exit pose during it, plus a 4-phase label (Approach/Entry/Traverse/Exit) derived from expert-path height trends
Multimodal temporal encoder: dual ImageNet ResNet-18 (RGB, depth) with gated fusion, history MLP, guidance embedding (Up/Down/Unknown), a 5-step context, and a Transformer encoder
Query-based affordance estimator: a learnable query cross-attends over the context to give h_aff, decoded by parallel pose regression and phase classification heads

Causal action decoder: autoregressive Transformer over FORWARD/LEFT/RIGHT/STOP sequences with h_aff as an extra memory token; beam search (5) reranked by likelihood and geometric residual to the predicted pose

Failure-aware preference refinement: 20 on-policy rounds with 2,048 rollouts each; deviation/failure detection, A* recovery to the expert route; deviation snippets paired with normal/recovery snippets; length- and snippet-normalized log-likelihood, Bradley-Terry style loss (β=1, λ=0.1) mixed with expert and on-policy imitation losses

Plug-and-play takeover: GroundingDINO detects stairs, the VLM gives relevance and direction; PACE takes control until the phase head predicts Exit or a budget limit is hit, then returns control and can be reactivated

setting.backbone: PACE: dual ResNet-18 + Transformer (27.4M params, trained); high-level VLM Qwen-3.6-27B-FP8 (frozen) inside six frozen zero-shot navigators
setting.training_data: R2R-CE-CF train (925 episodes) and RxR-CE-CF train (932 episodes) cross-floor episodes; expert stair trajectories plus 20 rounds of on-policy rollouts (2,048 each); pose/phase labels auto-derived
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with stair-direction guidance from the VLM
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / LEFT 30° / RIGHT 30° with STOP token per proposal
setting.privileged: none at test time (expert route and A* used only for training labels)

numbers.eval_set_note: cross-floor episodes (|h_s-h_g|>1 m) of R2R-CE val-unseen, 261 episodes; HSGM+PACE (best)
numbers.extra: PACE trained on the R2R-CE-CF train split; baselines rerun by the authors

numbers.eval_set_note: cross-floor en-US episodes of RxR-CE val-unseen, 217 episodes; HSGM+PACE (best)
numbers.extra: PACE trained on the RxR-CE-CF train split; baselines rerun by the authors

numbers_note: Results are on the authors' own cross-floor subsets (R2R-CE-CF, RxR-CE-CF), not standard full-split benchmarks. All six navigators were reported in Table 1; only HSGM and one other per benchmark are listed here. Averages: SR 16.35→27.65 (R2R-CE-CF) and 4.76→12.06 (RxR-CE-CF). Baseline-alone numbers are omitted.
results: Across six zero-shot navigators, PACE raises average SR on R2R-CE-CF from 16.35 to 27.65 (+11.30) and on RxR-CE-CF from 4.76 to 12.06 (+7.30). The strongest system, HSGM+PACE, reaches 50.19 SR (from 31.80) and 27.65 SR (from 9.68). Standalone stair-traversal ablations show PACE at 67.4 OSR vs 63.1 for waypoint conditioning, and a real Unitree Go2 completes a two-floor stairwell ascent.
limitations: Gains are local to stair transitions; NDTW gains are small and some SPL/NDTW cases are inconclusive or decrease (e.g. 3-step-Nav NDTW on RxR-CE-CF); PACE cannot fix wrong global direction or takeover never triggering

PACE is supervised on the benchmark train split, and takeover depends on GroundingDINO and VLM gating; premature Exit predictions (27.7% of Entry states misclassified as Approach) and harmful takeovers occur
Real-world evidence is a single qualitative stairwell case with left-right oscillation and reduced railing clearance; only stairs are handled
